ash_rules: Actions that create NotificationIntent MUST require explicit tenant context and actor or system_actor context.
Service actions MUST enforce idempotency with unique constraints on idempotency_key.
All reads of NotificationIntent by org actors MUST be scoped by org_id and MUST exclude sensitive variable values.

atlas.architect: NOTIF-1 isolates event-to-message orchestration from COMM rendering/dispatch, INT provider routing, and domain business truth.
atlas.assemble: Implementation MUST use Ash 3.x resources under Ticketing.Notifications and Oban queue notifications per OBQC-1.
atlas.link: NOTIF-1 links ORD-1/TKT-1/IAM-1/marketing events to COMM-1 MessageRequest without creating circular ownership or cross-domain writes.
atlas.stress_test: NOTIF-1 MUST fail closed on missing reactor, event schema mismatch, forbidden trigger scope, missing consent proof for marketing, variable mapping failure, COMM rejection, duplicate idempotency key, and safe-mode deferral.
atlas.trace: Every reactor run MUST carry source_event_id, org_id, actor_ref or system_actor_ref, correlation_id, reactor_id, template_id, template_version, consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 when required, and idempotency_key.

changes: Fixed refund-completed reactor source owner from ORD-1 to REFUND-1.
Replaced ambiguous dual-source owner references with IAM-2 for identity lifecycle notification source events.
Added controlled source/template/activation status fields and disabled all reactors that are pending source event, EVT registry, or template readiness.
Added hard sentinel and gates proving disabled reactors cannot create NotificationIntent records.
Kept post-purchase upsell marketing-only and CONSENT-gated.
Renamed test-gates artifact to BP-0 Test_Gates filename format.
Raised ERR-1, COMM-1, and INT-1 dependency floors to the coordinated clean versions.
Strengthened dependency-floor gates with explicit JSON pointer assertions.
Preserved NOTIF as thin orchestration authority without provider calls or business-truth mutation.
Initial CS-0@3.0.0 NOTIF-1 orchestration contract for domain-event-to-COMM message request mapping.
Replace invalid message_class=auth with COMM-compatible message_class=transactional plus trigger_category=auth.
Align source event names to versioned ticketing.*.v1 names and declare binding_status for upstream events not yet exported by their source contracts.
Replace non-canonical NotificationIntent statuses with canonical status atoms plus outcome_reason.
Add source event binding matrix to prevent hidden ORD/TKT/IAM/TRK event drift.
Add gates for COMM message-class parity, canonical intent statuses, and source event binding status.

change_log.summary: Final hardening: CS-compatible upper snake_case gate IDs, NOTIF->INT floor aligned to INT-1 v1.0.4, and self-failing sensitive-variable and banned-token gates removed or narrowed.

rules: Any reactor with message_class=marketing MUST require consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 produced by CONSENT-1 before creating a COMM MessageRequest.
NOTIF-1 MUST NOT downgrade a marketing purpose to transactional in order to bypass consent.
Cart abandonment, post-purchase upsell, winback, newsletter, and sales funnel messages MUST be marketing class by default.
Tracking tokens or campaign attribution links MUST be issued by TRK-1 and MUST carry consent proof where required.
Auth and account-recovery triggers MUST be message_class=transactional and trigger_category=auth; auth MUST NOT be introduced as a COMM message_class unless COMM-1 explicitly adds it later.

dependencies.reason: BP-0 defines the CS-0@3.0.0 blueprint discipline used by this bundle.
CS-0 defines the schema families and suite_schema target for this bundle.
TG-0 defines test-gate authoring conventions and deterministic assertion posture.
CG-0 defines strict CI expectations for bundle, manifest, dependency, and gate validation.
V42-0 supplies the constitutional tenancy, reliability, idempotency, and observability invariants.
TEN-1 governs org_id scoping, tenant context propagation, and cross-tenant denial.
IAM-1 governs actor identity, capabilities, step-up, and audited privileged operations.
ERR-1 governs canonical error envelope and stable NOTIF_* subcodes registered for NOTIF-1 v1.0.4 and later.
OBS-1 governs telemetry, alerts, runbooks, and SLO evidence.
OBQC-1 governs queue capacity, backpressure, and notification queue posture.
PSC-1 governs performance and safe-mode degradation requirements.
LOCKS-1 governs deterministic locking for publish, route resolution, and idempotent processing.
DATA-1 governs data classification, minimization, and retention posture.
COMM-1 owns templates, message requests, rendering, suppression, receipts, and dispatch semantics consumed by NOTIF-1.
NOTIF-1 relies on INT-1 v1.0.4 provider-routing floors while preserving the rule that NOTIF-1 never calls providers directly.
CONSENT-1 supplies consent proof hashes for marketing triggers and platform/org consent scope.
TRK-1 owns tracking tokens and campaign attribution when notification links include tracking behavior.
ORD-1 provides order finalized/paid/refunded event source references for transactional notification triggers.
TKT-1 provides ticket issued/revoked event source references for ticket delivery notification triggers.
REFUND-1 is the proper source contract for refund lifecycle notification triggers when refund events are made normative.

deterministic_uuid_sorting.rule: When NOTIF-1 hashes/signs audience lists, recipient lists, or source event UUID sets, it MUST normalize UUIDs to raw 16-byte form, sort by unsigned lexicographic byte order ascending, and MUST NOT sort UUID strings.

execution_rules: Reactors MUST run only after the source domain event commit is durable.
Reactors MUST enqueue NotificationIntent processing through Oban and MUST NOT run provider calls synchronously.
Checkout, payment, ledger, ticket issuance, auth, and order finalization MUST NOT wait for NOTIF or COMM delivery outcomes.
Safe mode MUST defer or drop marketing reactors first, then low-priority operational reactors, while preserving auth and transactional notification attempts as queued work when safe.

foundation_refs.reason: V42 requires all side effects to be idempotent, tenant-scoped, observable, and retried only through Oban.

invariants: NotificationIntent MUST be append-only for creation facts; state transitions MUST be audited or represented as append-only lifecycle events.
NotificationIntent.idempotency_key MUST be deterministic over canonical_json(org_id, source_event_id, reactor_id, recipient_ref, comm_template_id, comm_template_version).
The same idempotency_key MUST NOT submit more than one COMM MessageRequest.
NotificationIntent.status MUST use canonical status atoms only; outcome_reason carries blocked/deferred/comm_rejected semantics.
NotificationIntent MUST store redacted variables hash only and MUST NOT store raw reset tokens, invite tokens, ticket credentials, emails, phone numbers, or full rendered content.
A reactor definition MUST bind to exactly one source_event_name and exactly one COMM template pin.
A reactor definition MUST be disabled rather than deleted when historical notification traces exist.
A platform-scoped reactor MUST use platform_org_id consent scope when it creates marketing messages.
An org-scoped reactor MUST require org_id and MUST be protected by TEN-1 RLS.
trigger_category MAY describe auth/order/ticket/refund intent, but message_class MUST remain one of COMM-1 classes: transactional, marketing, operational, legal.
A reactor MUST NOT create NotificationIntent records unless reactor_activation_status=enabled.
A reactor may be enabled only when source_binding_status=active_registered and template_binding_status=active_template.
A transactional source event MAY trigger a marketing reactor only when message_class=marketing and consent_requirement=required.

boundary_rules: NOTIF-1 MUST be a thin orchestration contract and MUST NOT mutate ORD-1, TKT-1, IAM-1, PAY, or ledger business truth.
NOTIF-1 MUST create COMM-1 MessageRequest records asynchronously after authoritative domain events are committed.
NOTIF-1 MUST NOT send provider calls directly and MUST NOT use provider_account_ref except as read-only trace evidence received from COMM/INT outcomes.
NOTIF-1 MUST NOT include raw email, phone, reset token, invite token, ticket credential, or rendered message body in notification logs.

required_upstream_event_deltas.reason: Auth recovery needs a durable, non-enumerating event before NOTIF can send password reset messages.
User/org invitations need a durable event before NOTIF can send invitation messages.
TKT-1 declares ticketing.ticket.issued.v1, but NOTIF activation requires EVT-1 registry confirmation and an active COMM template binding.
Refund notification must trigger only after authoritative refund completion.
Cart abandonment is marketing and must be emitted only by a consent-aware tracking/funnel source.

rules: Reactors MUST NOT silently bind to unversioned or informal event names.
source_binding_status MUST be one of active_registered, disabled_pending_source_event, or disabled_pending_evt_registry.
template_binding_status MUST be one of active_template or disabled_pending_template.
reactor_activation_status MUST be enabled or disabled.
Any reactor whose reactor_activation_status is not enabled MUST NOT create NotificationIntent records.
A reactor may be enabled only when source_binding_status=active_registered and template_binding_status=active_template.
A transactional source event MAY trigger a marketing reactor only when message_class=marketing and consent_requirement=required.
Before implementation, every active reactor MUST either bind to a registered EVT-1/EVT-2 event or remain disabled.

standard_reactor_catalog.pii_safety: reset token MUST be passed to COMM as sensitive variable and MUST be redacted before NOTIF persistence
standard_reactor_catalog.disabled_reason: IAM-2 must export/register the source event and COMM template must be active before runtime execution.

standard_reactor_catalog.pii_safety: invite token MUST be redacted before NOTIF persistence
standard_reactor_catalog.disabled_reason: IAM-2 must export/register the source event and COMM template must be active before runtime execution.

standard_reactor_catalog.checkout_safety: COMM failure MUST NOT block order finalization
standard_reactor_catalog.disabled_reason: Source event is active, but COMM template binding is not yet active.

standard_reactor_catalog.ticket_safety: ticket credentials MUST be delivered by signed link by default and MUST NOT be logged by NOTIF
standard_reactor_catalog.disabled_reason: TKT-1 declares ticketing.ticket.issued.v1, but NOTIF activation requires EVT-1 registry confirmation and active COMM template binding.
REFUND-1 must export/register ticketing.refund.completed.v1 and COMM template must be active before runtime execution.

standard_reactor_catalog.marketing_safety: Cart abandonment MUST be marketing-only and MUST carry CONSENT-1 proof.
standard_reactor_catalog.disabled_reason: TRK-1 must export/register the consent-aware cart abandonment candidate event and COMM template must be active.

standard_reactor_catalog.marketing_safety: A transactional event MAY trigger a marketing reactor, but the resulting message MUST be marketing class and CONSENT-gated.
standard_reactor_catalog.disabled_reason: Source event is active, but COMM marketing template binding is not yet active.

summary: Notification orchestration reactor contract aligned to COMM-1 message classes and CS-0@3.0.0 structure.
title: NOTIF-1 — Notification Orchestration and Reactor Mapping Contract

rules: Variable mappings MUST be explicit allowlist transforms and MUST NOT pass entire domain event payloads into COMM.
Variable mappings MUST produce only COMM-1 allowed variable names and types for the pinned template version.
Variable mappings MUST redact sensitive tokens before NotificationIntent persistence and MUST provide only transient sensitive values to the COMM request boundary when COMM requires them.
Money values MUST be provided as money_minor plus currency_code_iso_4217 according to COMM-1 money_display_policy.
URLs MUST be url_https values and MUST be generated by the owning domain or TRK-1 when tracking is involved.
